"'The Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019' was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 11th December 2019. It is a landmark bill that seeks to provide for the processing of personal data in a manner that recognizes both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process personal data for lawful purposes. This is the first Act of the Parliament of India where "she/her" pronouns were used unlike the usual "he/him" pronouns.

Timeline

On 18 November 2022, the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) released the draft of the Data Protection Bill, 2022, which aims to replace the existing Information Technology (Reasonable security practices and procedures and sensitive personal data or information) Rules, 2011. The new bill focuses on the protection of personal data and provides for the processing of digital personal data in a manner that recognizes both the right of individuals to protect their personal data and the need to process personal data for lawful purposes, and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto”.

As it replaces the Information Technology Act, 2000, it also replaces the concept of information security with the right of an individual to control their personal data.

The Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019, draws inspiration from the European Union's General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and is built around the concept of "privacy by design." It introduces several new concepts, such as data fiduciaries, data principals, and significant data fiduciaries, and lays down the obligations of these entities in processing personal data.

The bill also introduces the concept of data localization, which requires certain categories of personal data to be stored and processed within India. This is intended to ensure that Indian citizens have control over their personal data and that it is not transferred to countries with inadequate data protection regimes.

The Personal Data Protection Bill, 2019, also includes provisions for the establishment of a Data Protection Authority, which will be responsible for enforcing the bill's provisions and ensuring that data fiduciaries comply with their obligations.
